assumptions: A sufficiently frequent subset of agency assets falls clearly within Article 50 transparency duties.
Agencies need evidence beyond the labels and logs supplied by their generation and publishing platforms.
Relevant provenance and disclosure state can be inspected reliably at final approval.
A local-first or metadata-only design can meet agency security expectations.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid agency pilots showing covered-asset frequency, real metadata-loss rates across named tool chains, legal-review time avoided, evidence acceptance, security approval, renewal intent, and resistance to native-platform substitution.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Checking provenance and disclosures at final creative approval addresses the practical gap created when multi-tool editing and publishing chains strip or transform machine-readable marks.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Article 50 creates real per-asset compliance work for covered content, but scope varies and there is no evidence that agencies will buy a separate ledger rather than use policy, counsel, or native tools.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Workspace licensing and metered evidence events can have low compute cost, but integration churn, sensitive-asset security, legal maintenance, onboarding, and channel costs make the proposed margin uncertain.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: EU agencies generate high asset volumes, yet the proposal does not identify one agency segment and asset class with frequent unambiguous Article 50 exposure and budget ownership.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Generative platforms, creative suites, digital asset managers, and publishers are natural provenance owners and can incorporate marking, logs, and approval evidence into existing subscriptions.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven cross-tool evidence layer could expand across media types, publication destinations, client approval portals, and jurisdictions, although each adds policy and integration complexity.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A permissioned corpus of tool-chain failures could improve checks, but the company owns neither source assets nor platform integrations and native standards may reduce the distinctive data.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder fits metadata and lineage automation, but has no agency workflow access, production integration, proprietary corpus, compliance authority, or brand trust.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Article 50 obligations are newly applicable and official guidance plus industry signatories create an immediate workflow-change window for covered content.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Compliance advisers, insurers, and production-tool integrations are plausible routes, but none is secured and the most powerful platforms have incentives to bundle rather than refer.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A local preflight is buildable, but scope classification, metadata survival, tool churn, sensitive campaign assets, legal representations, and security obligations create high operational risk.

highest_value_structural_change: Launch as a local-first approval gate for one clearly covered asset class, distributed through a signed legal or insurer channel and integrated with the agency's existing DAM without retaining source assets.
main_structural_strength: A newly enforceable obligation maps to a high-frequency, auditable per-asset approval event, and vendor-neutral checking can catch failures created between otherwise compliant tools.
primary_score_limiter: The venture lacks control of creative and publication integrations while those platforms are best positioned to bundle the same marking and evidence functionality.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Not every AI-assisted asset is covered, equivalent compliance routes are allowed, and dominant creative and generation platforms can preserve provenance and logs natively at little incremental customer cost.
